title: Shard-aware packetization and adaptive kernel switchover to reduce embedding endpoint tail latency
creator: Lena Martinez
description:
Problem: Embedding endpoint p99 and p99.9 latency spikes correlate with uneven per-shard compute packing and delayed kernel selection for heterogeneous request mixes (varying sequence lengths and model variants). We frequently see a small number of in-flight requests monopolize GPU streams and force fallback to slower kernels, causing long tails that hurt user-facing reranking latency.

Goal: Implement a shard-aware packetization layer plus an adaptive kernel switchover policy to reduce 99th+ percentile latency without materially degrading throughput. The approach should be conservative (no availability regressions) and fully observable through new telemetry and dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: A/B result: p99 latency for embeddings endpoint reduced by >=15% on production-like workload
p99.9 latency reduced by >=25% under the bursty reranking trace
End-to-end throughput impact <= 2% loss for standard steady-state load
Canary rollout with automatic rollback on error-rate increase > 0.5% or tail regressions
New dashboards and traces available showing per-shard queue depth, selected kernel, and packetization buckets
notes: Proposed name: 'shard-packetizer' for the runtime component. This pairs with a small adaptive policy that flips kernels when per-request wait time exceeds a budget and a predicted kernel switch will reduce remaining compute time. Quantile-aware admission control will be implemented to dampen jitter by preferentially delaying very large requests when they would push a shard beyond its quantile latency target. Avoids global request drops. Security review not required for changes; will add config flags behind an operator-enabled feature gate.
steps: Instrument runtime: emit per-shard metrics (queue depth, inflight compute weight, current kernel id) — PR # (draft)
Implement packetizer: compute lightweight weight estimate (seq_len * model_cost_coeff), group incoming requests into packets by shard to balance estimated weight
Add adaptive kernel policy: monitor wait time per request and initiate safe switchover to alternate kernel or quantized variant when predicted remaining time < threshold
Create e2e benchmark harness using replay of reranking trace (60m) and bursty traces; measure p50/p95/p99/p99.9
Run offline simulation against production traces to pick admission thresholds and kernel switch heuristics
Create canary rollout plan and dashboard, implement feature flag, and write operator runbook for rollback
Merge changes behind feature flag, run progressive canaries (5% -> 25% -> 100%) and monitor
updates: 2026-02-25: Ticket created after spike analysis — linked to recent reranking regressions seen in /dashboards/embeddings/rerank-latency
2026-02-28: Prototype packetizer implemented in sandbox runtime. Initial microbench: p99 improved 9% on synthetic uniform load. PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2457
2026-03-03: Added per-shard telemetry to staging. Observed that 3% of shards consistently had >2x inflight weight relative to cluster median during rerank bursts

2026-03-06: Adaptive kernel switch algorithm drafted — linear model to predict remaining kernel time from measured KV-cache hits and sequence length. Simulation shows p99.9 reduction estimate of ~22% when combined with packetizer

2026-03-10: Began offline replay of 60m production rerank trace using harness: first run shows p99 down 12% and p99.9 down 18%. Need further tuning of admission thresholds and guardrails before canary
